scope: Result representation after typed computation. Single-scale and mixed-scale expression rules supersede unrestricted automatic ladder selection.

acceptedExample.notation: Ungrouped Latin examples with decimal dot are semantic examples, not an override of locale, spacing or grouping rules.

preserve: working value, dimensional type and semantic context
canChange: display unit scale and its corresponding displayed numeric coefficient
explicitConversionTarget: existing explicit target-unit choice has precedence over automatic choice; no automatic rescaling away from a requested target
displayPipeline: typed calculation and applicable reference-number operations
explicit target, or scale selected under the latest expression-context rules; unresolved general policies must not be treated as defaults
format the coefficient in that unit under the existing decimal and approximate-zero rules
group identical displayed answers under existing rules
copy: Displayed coefficient only for an ordinary measured quantity, including fixed duration. In the accepted examples 2m copies 2, 1100mm copies 1100 and 1.1m copies 1.1 before locale/grouping formatting. Percentage and calendar exceptions remain applicable.
lazyAlternatives: retain typed alternatives and choose display for each before grouping; do not change unit inference merely to obtain a convenient scale
history: existing immutable working values and displayed answers remain authoritative; copying history does not recalculate or rerun a new live scale decision
locale: existing Latin/local unit notation and explicit target-spelling rules remain applicable
unresolved: General adequate-scale ranking among multiple user-supplied scales, including mixed families and repeated use of values.
Reconciliation of preserved input scales with floor/round, fixed-duration and derived-numerator examples; the role of full ladders when scale context is absent.
latestDecision: User amendment after round 29 limits result-scale choice to scales supplied in the expression; explicit conversion still wins.

scaleSourceRules.explicitTarget: Use the requested target for the expression it covers under existing operator precedence.
scaleSourceRules.singleScale: Preserve the scale explicitly used by the user when it was not mixed with another scale.
scaleSourceRules.mixedScales: Choose among scales participating in the expression; 1m + 100mm must display 1100mm.
scaleSourceRules.generalMixedScaleRanking: Pending round 30; do not infer a universal ranking from the accepted example alone.
scaleSourceRules.effectOnInference: Do not choose a latent metre/minute interpretation merely to obtain a preferred display scale.

previousAutomaticPolicy.status: Initially accepted in round 29, then superseded wherever it conflicts with the user amendment. These ladders are not an active unrestricted candidate pool.
previousAutomaticPolicy.ranking: Largest scale with absolute coefficient at least 1, smallest scale below the ladder, no hard 1000 upper cap.
previousAutomaticPolicy.mixedPhysicalFamilies: Metric output for mixed metric/nonmetric or US/UK gallon families.
previousAutomaticPolicy.informationFamilies: Preserve bit/byte and decimal/binary family; use first participating measurement when mixed; bare b/B are decimal; no context defaults to decimal bytes.
previousAutomaticPolicy.noFamilyContext: Metric output, or decimal bytes for information.
previousAutomaticPolicy.postRoundingPromotion: Reformat from the working value if display rounding reaches the next scale; the new candidate constraint cannot be bypassed.

zero: Exact zero preserves the unit of the expression semantic context, or the type base unit without context. Never depend on previous displayed answers or history.

derivedDenominator.preserve: Result denominator context; first participating measurement when denominator units are mixed; selected-value context for min/max.
derivedDenominator.numeratorScale: Subject to the latest expression-scale constraint; generalized treatment is pending round 30.

separateFormats: Temperature, angles, percentages and calendar values retain their separately accepted formats. A calendar period with nonzero months retains compound output and full-unit copying.
